$comment: Journey 7.16 — start-up time and bundle size within a budget.
Every number here was measured, and each says HOW. Nothing is inherited.
Raising a ceiling is a deliberate, reviewable diff: check-startup-budget.mjs only
enforces it, it never edits it.

bundle.howMeasured: node scripts/check-startup-budget.mjs — runs node node_modules/expo/bin/cli export --platform android and takes the size in bytes of the single .hbc under _expo/static/js/android
bundle.$ceilingNote: measured + 10%. The gate fails above this and warns within 5% of it.

$comment: NOT comparable with the figure above, and the difference is not a defect.
This is assets/index.android.bundle inside the last locally built release APK
It is a Gradle/Hermes release build, three days and 68 mobile commits behind the
export above (+12,750 lines). The next release build is what will let the two be
🔴 What is NOT measured, so no one reads this as a full picture: the member's real
cold start on a shipped build. adb's `am start -W` stops at the first frame, which
for this app is the native splash — it reported ~1.3s while the JavaScript had not
finished loading. React Native's own reactNativeStartupTiming marks would answer it
from the native side but are undefined in this Expo SDK build (measured on a device
2026-08-23). Sentry is now configured in production, but no cold-start trace from a
store-distributed build has been observed. The JavaScript phase below remains the
only cold-start timing this workspace can honestly prove today.

nativeFirstFrameMs.howMeasured: adb shell am start -W -n ie.project.nexus/.MainActivity, TotalTime, three cold starts after am force-stop
nativeFirstFrameMs.$note: The native splash frame only. Kept because it is the figure people quote, and it is the figure that misleads.

jsPhaseMs.howMeasured: lib/startupTiming.ts logs `nexus-startup: … js <n>ms` at the root layout's first commit; read from adb logcat on emulator-5554 (411dp, API 36) after am force-stop, three cold starts
jsPhaseMs.$buildTypeNote: A debug build downloads its bundle from Metro and Hermes must parse JavaScript rather than load bytecode, so a release build should be FASTER than this. Treat it as an upper bound on the JavaScript phase.
jsPhaseMs.$note: Measured from the bundle entry point, which is why index.js exists. Timed from the root layout instead, this read 0ms while the app took seconds to open.
